comments.body:
> 'MD_DynamicRelease' doesn't match value 'MDd_DynamicDebug'

That's your issue. Some conflict between _some_ libraries being built in Release mode and _some_ in Debug mode.

Can you try maybe those two?

```
cmake --build build --config Release
```

and

```
cmake --build build --config Debug
```

cmake --build build --config Debug

Produced the same output as before, which seems to confirm that it built Debug config by default

cmake --build build --config Release

Produces the following output:

    D:\MAVSDK\examples\takeoff_and_land>cmake --build build --config Release
    Microsoft (R) Build Engine version 17.2.1+52cd2da31 for .NET Framework
    Copyright (C) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.
    
    mavsdk.lib(system_impl.obj) : error LNK2019: unresolved external symbol __std_find_trivial_8 referenced in function "class     mavsdk::PluginImplBase * * __cdecl __std_find_trivial<class mavsdk::PluginImplBase *,class mavsdk::PluginImplBase *>(class mavsdk::PluginImplBase * *,class ma
    vsdk::PluginImplBase * *,class mavsdk::PluginImplBase * const)" (??$__std_find_trivial@PEAVPluginImplBase@mavsdk@@PEAV12@@@YAPEAPEAVPluginImplBase@mavsdk@@PEAPEAV01@0QEAV01@@Z) [D:\MAVSDK\examples\takeoff_and_land\build\takeoff_and_land.vcxproj]
    D:\MAVSDK\examples\takeoff_and_land\build\Release\takeoff_and_land.exe : fatal error LNK1120: 1 unresolved externals [D:\MAVSDK\examples\takeoff_and_land\build\takeoff_and_land.vcxproj]

Much better! So the MAVSDK you installed is a Release version, meaning that you should build your example in Release mode.

Now I suspect that you are trying to build an example from the `main` branch, but you installed MAVSDK 1.4.x. That would usually work, but we are in the process of moving to MAVSDK v2, meaning that `main` is not compatible with `1.x.x`.

Can you try to build the `takeoff_and_land` example from https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/tree/v1.4.6 (instead of the one from `main`?

MAVSDK 1.4.6 is the one I have been using.

I think I stumbled on the cause and then accidently fixed it.

Bottom line is: It now builds and runs!

I think it was an issue with the Visual Studio 2022 version I was using. 

I found the following issue report indicating that others had the same problem about a month ago, and isolated it to a VS 2022 update: (https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/6091)

So, I updated my Visual Studio 2022, tried again, and it worked.

Thanks again for your help!!!

Now I can move on to the real challenge - learning to use it.
Just a comment: make sure never to match Release and Debug builds on Windows as the ABI of std::string is not compatible.

issue.title: add_any_connection not working as intended

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
Currently trying to get some of the examples to run on my Windows 11 system and haven't been successful.

I'm building the examples with the local install of MAVSDK (from mavsdk-windows-x64-release) rather then building from source, and including the mavsdk.dll in the same directory as the executable for each example. When trying to run each example as intended ex: "./build/Debug/gimbal_device_tester.exe udpin://0.0.0.0:14540" Ill get an error saying that the protocol / connection URL is invalid, and when switching to "udpin://:14540" the error doesn't appear, but when `add_any_connection` is called during execution it hangs indefinitely, and eventually causes the program to abort with no indication of why this is happening.

Same behavior is observed running other examples such as: takeoff_and_land, autopilot_server, etc.

timeline.body: Just a comment: make sure never to match Release and Debug builds on Windows as the ABI of std::string is not compatible.
